name: WELLS, the Hon. Anika Shay

headline.note: Primary material identifies early kitchen-assistant work and Joe Ludwig office service observed in2010. Public professional profile gives Griffith2004–2009 and Maurice Blackburn August2014–May2019; a contemporary parliamentary directory identifies Wells as Ludwig's Assistant Adviser. Hours and leave remain unknown; political staff excluded and headline totals remain null.

career_spells.employer: Residential aged-care facility, employer not identified
career_spells.role: Kitchen assistant in residential aged care
career_spells.evidence_note: A biographical profile reports that Wells worked part-time at the residential aged-care facility where her mother worked. The employer, dates, role, ownership, hours and leave are not identified. First-person September 2022 speech confirms unqualified kitchen assistant work in Daisy wing approximately twenty years earlier. Approximate recollection is not converted into a start year; HammondCare hosted the speech but is not established as her employer.
career_spells.counting_note: The part-time work is retained as an unresolved early employment lead; no sector or duration can be calculated.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Laws and Bachelor of Arts student
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records the Griffith degrees. Wells' public professional profile gives Griffith University2004–2009, while the university alumni profile specifically dates both completions to2009. Public biographies also record an Australian National University graduate diploma and admission to legal practice in2012. Exact enrolment days, study load and employment overlaps are not published. ANU diploma is separated below; legal admission does not establish diploma completion.

career_spells.employer: Australian Government ministerial office or offices, not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional biographies report five years as a Labor adviser in the federal government before Wells joined Maurice Blackburn in 2014. They do not identify the office or offices, titles, exact boundaries, hours or leave. A start year is therefore not inferred from the stated duration. Ludwig office is now identified in a nested spell below. The umbrella five-year duration remains unsplit; the 2014 next-job start is not proof of prior payroll cessation. Other employing offices and gaps remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded from the public/private headline totals.

career_spells.role: Lawyer specialising in workers' compensation and road-injury matters
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records legal work at Maurice Blackburn from 2014 to 2019. Wells' first speech describes private-sector workers' compensation practice, and party biographies add representation of people injured at work or on the road. The exact commencement, payroll cessation, hours, leave and campaign arrangements are not published; 18 May 2019 is an outer bound from election, not a proved employment endpoint. Public professional index gives August 2014–May 2019; these reported month boundaries supersede the earlier election-day proxy. No actual day, full-time label, maternity leave, campaign leave or overlap conclusion is available. The official Political Exchange Council report names her as Maurice Blackburn lawyer in the July–August2018delegation list. It does not establish leave/payroll status during travel.
career_spells.counting_note: Private legal employment is supported, but exact boundaries and substantive full-time evidence are insufficient.

career_spells.evidence_note: A 2020 profile says Wells co-founded the local Chermside parkrun in mid-2015. It describes community volunteering, not paid employment; a cessation date is not supplied.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Lilley
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records election for Lilley in 2019 and re-election in 2022; the frozen Parliamentary Handbook records continuing service and subsequent re-election in 2025.

career_spells.role: Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice student
career_spells.evidence_note: Qualification reported; actual enrolment/completion unknown. Admission in 2012 is not substituted for graduation.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: Office of Senator Joe Ludwig, Australian Government
career_spells.role: Assistant adviser; media contact observed 21 May 2010
career_spells.evidence_note: A contemporary parliamentary directory lists Wells as an Assistant Adviser in Ludwig's office, and a 21May2010 joint ministerial release names her as a media contact. Ludwig later confirms her among former staff. The directory and dated observation are not commencement or cessation evidence. Nested within the existing five-year political-staff umbrella; do not add durations.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: Australian Political Exchange Council delegation; host American Council of Young Political Leaders
career_spells.role: Leader, thirty-fourth Australian delegation to United States
career_spells.evidence_note: Official report supplies delegation travel interval and names Wells leader. These are exchange-activity dates, not appointment to paid employment. No salary, law-firm paid/unpaid leave, campaign break or concurrent work arrangements supplied.
career_spells.counting_note: Political exchange participation excluded; no additional headline employment years or automatic subtraction from legal employment.

Obtain exact Griffith University and Australian National University study dates, legal-admission evidence and any employment overlap.
Identify every federal ministerial office, title and exact boundary in the reported five years of Labor advisory work; obtain hours and leave while retaining political staff as excluded.
